title: Certify fixed-basis R420 target matching and the eight-ADD gap
body:
This contribution certifies the optimal disjoint target pairing for PR #694's fixed helper basis and applies it to PR #681's R420 construction.

Results:

- Complete local cost: 18,362 ADDs
- Published #681: 18,378 ADDs
- Existing #733 matching on the same #681 body: 18,370 ADDs
- New incremental saving: eight ADDs beyond that existing recipe

A 58-pair witness and 120 integer vertex prices certify the exact saving of 1,442 within this fixed-basis pairing class. All 7,140 edge inequalities and equality of the primal/dual totals are checked without relying on a numerical solver.

Recorded validation:

- Exact reconstruction of the #681 predecessor receipt
- Forward/reverse checks on all 660 inputs and restoration controls
- Separate matrix-based verification and certificate mutation tests
- Fresh native 5/9/11-stage and hosted replays comparing published #681 with this replacement
- Relocation and corruption checks

The #733 matching on the same #681 body is checked locally; a separate native/hosted replay for that comparator is not claimed.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-optimal-composed-pairs/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/r420-optimal-composed-pairs/independent_check.py
```

Local precision remains 104 bits. Hosted precision remains 196 bits charged at 256; two-level precision remains 432 charged at 512. This establishes neither a new kappa nor global circuit optimality. All inherited assumptions remain; the selected frontier and `upstream/` are unchanged.

See `research/r420-optimal-composed-pairs/README.md` and `research/r420-optimal-composed-pairs/VALIDATION.md` for pinned sources, predecessor credits, complete checks and limitations.

Prepared for Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, under Apache-2.0.
